findings.label: B4/E15 list or packed sentence
examples: It may, of course, be your inner child, mad that it’s taken you so long to come back, or it may be your inherited parent script, or something from earlier in th
findings.reason: The possibilities are the card he approved (IC-A14): the inner child, the parent script, something from earlier in the day, or a bit of each. They have different shapes (the child with why it is mad, "it may be" for the script) and end on his catch-all.

findings.label: D9 follows the source order
examples: 1/1 paragraphs follow the source's points in its order (agreement 1.00); fine if each part notices something; check T13 and T09 in the tell ledger
findings.reason: It is Emulate's rewrite of the two sentences it replaces, so it follows their points in order by design; the turns are Emulate's own ("what/where it is", "make sure to", "of course", "it may be").

findings.label: E125 list of three: an AI pattern in general (Joel 2026-10-03: "lists of 3 in general are an ai pattern"; 2026-10-07: "lists in general are overused by AI. try to avoid that unless it's really needed"). If the meaning doesn't need all three, drop the one that matters least; if it does, split them into sentences, the way he fixed P1 ("Maybe it just has something to say."), or give the items different shapes and end on a catch-all, the way he fixed Borrowed Adulthood P2 ("Other jobs can go to friends or community, outsource to the tools or pros, whatever works."). Joel, 01:06: "when there's no actual need for 3 items you can remove one of them"
examples: or it may be your inherited parent script, or
findings.reason: The linter's own exception: the list ends on a casual catch-all, his "or a bit of each" from IC-A14, the card he approved (so a REVIEW, not a FAIL); the possibilities are that card's meaning, the things the reaction may be.
